query: Our Seam.elm has grown to ~200 tiny one-off helpers after running the autofix. How do I clean it up and cut the clutter?
expected_behavior: Reframes Seam as a centralized design-system maintenance surface, not clutter to minimize. Triages each entry via the three paths: develop a new typed pattern (for recurring escapes — the deduped, pattern-encoding names show which primitive is missing), fix it at the call site (one-off / misuse / DS bug), or extend the DS to allow a legitimate need. Explains the count trends toward zero as the DS matures and is a measure of DS-fighting, not a target. Does NOT recommend reverting/suppressing/deleting to shrink Seam for its own sake, though it may name the suppress call-site-context tradeoff honestly.

query: Should I run ExtractToSeam across the whole app to consolidate every escape into Seam?
expected_behavior: Describes the census (allowedModules pointed at the seam module) as a deliberate DIAGNOSTIC sweep to see the full scope and prioritize — deterministic and regenerable, cheap to run and cheap to throw away — not a state to commit and forget. Notes hundreds of helpers measure how hard feature code fights the DS. Mentions punts (captured bindings, top-level values, point-free) are surfaced for manual handling, not auto-lifted. Does not treat the consolidated pile as the finished goal.

query: The gate flags Seam.asAttribute in my feature module as a seam escape outside allowed modules. Can I just add my module to allowedModules to make it go away?
expected_behavior: Says no — adding a feature module to the allow-list defeats the boundary (it lets that module escape freely). The allow-list is for genuine adapter/seam modules only. Directs to triage the escape instead: lift it into the seam (ExtractToSeam), fix it at the call site, or extend the DS. Does not recommend an elm-review-disable comment or widening the allow-list to silence a real, fixable escape.

query: I need a component admitted where a different kind is expected — is there a named, config-declared crossing for that, or do I have to use recast?
expected_behavior: Says there is no second, named crossing mechanism — recast is the one sanctioned brand escape, gated by NoSeamOutsideAllowedModules; each use discards a type guarantee. Points to the two real routes for a kind-crossing need: widen the relevant `admits` list directly in config when that doesn't conflict with the design system's own guidance, or reach for recast (behind a seam module) when it genuinely does conflict and needs an explicit, reviewed exception. If asked, notes elm-cem briefly had a config-declared `_coerce` block emitting named crossings into a `<Lib>.Coerce` module that lived outside the seam gate, and it was removed because it duplicated recast's job with a narrower, ungated escape. Frames seams as sanctioned holes built on the fenced forges (HtmlIr.Internal / *.Unsafe).

query: A helper ExtractToSeam lifted reads `asAttribute (attribute "aria-hidden" "true")` and won't compile — attribute resolves to the wrong thing. Also I see TA.name undefined in Seam. What's going on?
expected_behavior: Recognizes these as the lift's cross-file re-qualification cases and routes to reference/lift-mechanics.md: an unqualified imported value whose bare name also names a seam top-level is re-qualified so it can't rebind (attribute -> Html.Attributes.attribute); a qualified ref whose module the seam imports under a different alias is re-qualified (TA.name -> TypedHtml.Attributes.name), not re-imported. Stresses that the integration build (does the lifted Seam compile?) is the ground truth, not the text-only Review.Test suite.
